title: SSH, keys and copying files
summary: Log in with keys instead of passwords, configure hosts, and move files with scp and rsync.

steps.title: SSH and key pairs
body: `ssh user@host` opens an encrypted shell on another machine (port 22). Log in with a **key pair** rather than a password:
ssh-copy-id ana@web1.example.com          # appends the .pub to the server's ~/.ssh/authorized_keys
ssh ana@web1.example.com                  # now logs in with the key
The private key never leaves your machine. The first connection asks you to confirm the server's **host key** fingerprint and saves it in `~/.ssh/known_hosts`.

steps.prompt: You connect and see `WARNING: REMOTE HOST IDENTIFICATION HAS CHANGED!`. What does it mean, and what should you do?
options: The server's host key differs from known_hosts: confirm with the server's owner (rebuild? or attack?) before removing the old entry with `ssh-keygen -R host`
Your private key expired: run ssh-keygen again
steps.explain: It's either a rebuilt server (common) or a man-in-the-middle (rare but real). Verify out of band, then `ssh-keygen -R host`.

steps.prompt: Where does each file live, and should it ever be shared?
buckets: Safe to share / put on servers

steps.title: ~/.ssh/config
body: Stop typing long commands. Save them as aliases:
ProxyJump bastion       # hop through the bastion
`ssh web1` now means `ssh -p 2222 -i ~/.ssh/deploy_ed25519 deploy@10.20.0.11`. For each setting, the **first** matching `Host` block that sets it wins, so put specific hosts first and `Host *` last.

steps.prompt: Run a command on a server on port 2222 with a specific key, without opening an interactive shell.
steps.explain: ssh takes a lowercase `-p` for the port (scp uses capital `-P`!), `-i` for the identity file, and runs a trailing command instead of a shell.

steps.title: Copying: scp and rsync
body: scp -P 2222 -r dist/ deploy@host:/srv/www/   # capital -P for port, -r recursive
rsync -avz dist/ web1:/srv/www/              # copy only what changed
rsync -avz --delete dist/ web1:/srv/www/     # also delete files removed locally (mirror)
rsync -avzn --delete dist/ web1:/srv/www/    # -n: dry run, show what it WOULD do
**The trailing slash matters**: `rsync dist/ dest` copies the *contents* of dist; `rsync dist dest` creates `dest/dist`.

steps.prompt: `dist` contains `index.html`. You run `rsync -a dist web1:/srv/www/`. What path does index.html end up at on web1?
steps.explain: Without a trailing slash on the source, rsync copies the directory itself. `dist/` would give `/srv/www/index.html`.

pairs: Mirror a build folder to a server, removing stale files
Preview what that mirror would change

steps.title: Resolve an ssh config alias
prompt: Write `(string Host, string User, int Port) SshResolve(List<string> config, string alias, string localUser)` that resolves `ssh alias` from `~/.ssh/config` lines:
- A `Host` line starts a block; it lists one or more patterns separated by spaces. Support exact names and `*` (matches everything).
- Inside matching blocks, read `HostName`, `User`, `Port` (keywords are case-insensitive). The **first** value found for each key wins.
- Defaults: host = the alias itself, user = `localUser`, port = 22. Ignore blank lines and `#` comments.
starter: (string Host, string User, int Port) SshResolve(List<string> config, string alias, string localUser)
solution: (string Host, string User, int Port) SshResolve(List<string> config, string alias, string localUser)
string key = parts[0].ToLowerInvariant(), val = parts.Length > 1 ? parts[1].Trim() : "";
if (key == "host") { active = val.Split(' ', StringSplitOptions.RemoveEmptyEntries).Any(p => p == "*" || p == alias); continue; }
hints: Track whether the current block matches with a bool, updated at each `Host` line.
`??=` assigns only when still null: exactly "first value wins".
template: var dojoCfg = new List<string> { "# my hosts", "Host web1 web1.prod", "    HostName 10.20.0.11", "    User deploy", "    Port 2222", "", "Host *", "    User ana", "    Port 22022" };
Dojo.Eq("second pattern on the Host line", ("10.20.0.11", "deploy", 2222), SshResolve(dojoCfg, "web1.prod", "me"));
Dojo.Eq("defaults with empty config", ("x", "me", 22), SshResolve(new List<string>(), "x", "me"));
